To understand how search engines work, imagine the Internet as a massive, endless library. In this library, every website is like a book, and each individual web page is a specific page within that book. If you are looking for a specific piece of information, you wouldn't want to read every book from cover to cover. Instead, you would use the library's index or catalog system to quickly locate the exact book and page that contains what you need. Search engines like Google function as this digital index, helping you navigate the vast library of the Internet to find the precise website and page that holds the information you are seeking.
